    #Tutorial 1 (Single-Phase A.C. Circuits)

    #Question 1

    Assume the loads are connected in parallel.

    #Part (a)

    Impedance of each load,

    Zˉlamp​=960∠0° Ω

    Zˉfan​=345∠53.13° Ω

    Zˉaircon​=482+362​∠tan−14836​=60∠36.87° Ω

    Impedance of combined load,

    Zˉeq​1​=Zˉ1​8​+Zˉ2​3​+Zˉ3​2​

    Zˉeq​1​=960∠0°8​+345∠53.13°3​+60∠36.87°2​

    Zˉeq​1​=9608​∠0°+3453​∠−53.13°+602​∠−36.87°

    Zˉeq​1​=0.040217−j0.026957

    Yˉeq​=0.048416∠−33.833° S

    Zˉeq​=20.654∠33.833° Ω

    #Part (b)

    Consider V as the reference voltage, Vˉ=240∠0°.

    Total complex current,

    Vˉ=IˉZˉeq​

    Iˉ=20.654∠33.833°240∠0°​

    Iˉ=11.620∠−33.833° A

    Power factor of combined load,

    PF=cosφ

    PF=cos33.833°

    PF=0.83066

    Negative phase difference indicates that current lags voltage.
    Since current lags voltage, the overall power factor is lagging.

    Total complex power,

    Sˉ=VˉIˉ∗

    Sˉ=240∠0°×11.620∠33.833°

    Sˉ=2788.8∠33.833° VA (polar form)

    Sˉnew​=2516.9∠33.833° VA (polar form)

    Sˉnew​=2090.7+j1401.3 VA (rectangular form)

    % change in current,

    %I=11.62011.039−11.620​=−5%

    % change in complex power,

    %S=2788.82516.9−2788.8​=−9.75%

    #Question 2

    Assume the loads are connected in parallel.

    #Part (a)

    Complex power of each load,

    Sˉmotor​=15∠cos−10.7=15∠45.573° kVA

    Sˉaircon​=5∠cos−10.8=5∠36.870° kVA

    Sˉothers​=0.853​∠cos−10.85=3.5294∠31.788° kVA

    Note that Sˉ is the product of reference voltage Vˉ and conjugate of Iˉ.
    For a lagging power factor, it is given as     Iˉ=I∠−θ→Iˉ∗=I∠θ.
    Thus, the phase difference of complex power is positive.

    Total complex power,

    SˉT​=Sˉmotor​+Sˉaircon​+Sˉothers​

    SˉT​=(15∠45.573°)+(5∠36.870°)+(3.5294∠31.788°)

    SˉT​=17.5+j15.571

    SˉT​=23.424∠41.662° kVA

    Overall power triangle,

    P=17.5 kW (real part)

    Q=15.6 kVAR (imaginary part)

    Total complex current,

    SˉT​=VˉIˉ∗

    Iˉ∗=240∠0°23424∠41.662°​

    Iˉ∗=97.6∠41.662°

    Iˉ=97.6∠−41.662° A

    Power factor of the plant,

    PF=cosφ

    PF=cos41.662°

    PF=0.74708 (lag)

    #Part (b)

    Impedance of capacitor,

    ZˉC​=XC​∠−90°=2πfC1​∠−90°

    ZˉC​=2π(50)(550×10−6)1​∠−90°

    ZˉC​=5.7875∠−90° Ω

    Complex current through capacitor,

    Vˉ=IˉC​ZˉC​

    IˉC​=5.7875∠−90°240∠0°​

    IˉC​=41.469∠90° A

    Complex power of capacitor,

    SˉC​=VˉIˉC​∗

    SˉC​=240∠0°×41.469∠−90°

    SˉC​=9952.6∠−90° VA (polar form)

    SˉC​=0−j9952.6 VA (rectangular form)

    Total complex power,

    SˉT​=Sˉmotor​+Sˉaircon​+Sˉothers​+SˉC​

    SˉT​=(17.5+j15.571)+(0−j9.9526)

    SˉT​=17.5+j5.6184

    SˉT​=18.380∠17.8° kVA

    Total complex current,

    SˉT​=VˉIˉ∗

    Iˉ∗=240∠0°18380∠17.8°​

    Iˉ∗=76.583∠17.8°

    Iˉ=76.583∠−17.8° A

    Power factor of the plant,

    PF=cosφ

    PF=cos17.8°

    PF=0.952 (lag)

    #Part (c)

    Total complex current,

    Iˉ1​=97.6∠−41.662° A (without capacitor)

    Iˉ2​=76.583∠−17.8° A (with capacitor)

    Scenario 1: without capacitor

    Complex power loss,

    Sˉloss​=Iˉ2Zˉcable​

    Sˉloss,1​=(97.6)2(0.15811)∠tan−10.050.15​

    Sˉloss,1​=1506.1∠71.565°

    Sˉloss,1​=476.27+j1428.8 VA

    Total complex power,

    Sˉ1​=Sˉmotor​+Sˉaircon​+Sˉothers​+Sˉloss,1​

    Sˉ1​=(17.5+j15.571)+(0.47627+j1.4288)

    Sˉ1​=17.976+j17

    Sˉ1​=24.741∠43.402° kVA

    Source voltage,

    Sˉ1​=Vˉs1​Iˉ1​∗

    Vˉs1​=97.6∠41.662°24741∠43.402°​

    Vˉs1​=253.49∠1.74° V

    Scenario 2: with capacitor

    Complex power loss,

    Sˉloss,2​=(76.583)2(0.15811)∠tan−10.050.15​

    Sˉloss,2​=927.33∠71.565°

    Sˉloss,2​=293.25+j879.74 VA

    Total complex power,

    Sˉ2​=Sˉmotor​+Sˉaircon​+Sˉothers​+SˉC​+Sˉloss,2​

    Sˉ2​=(17.5+j5.6184)+(0.29325+j0.87974)

    Sˉ2​=17.793+j6.4981

    Sˉ2​=18.942∠20.062° kVA

    Source voltage,

    Sˉ2​=Vˉs2​Iˉ2​∗

    Vˉs2​=76.583∠17.8°18942∠20.062°​

    Vˉs2​=247.35∠2.262° V

    Active power loss,

    Ploss,1​=476.27 W (without capacitor)

    Ploss,2​=293.25 W (with capacitor)

    #Tutorial 2 (Three-Phase A.C. Systems 1)

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    Phase voltage,

    VL​=3​VP​

    VP​=3​440​

    VP​=254.03 V

    Phase voltages,

    Vˉa​=254.03∠0° V

    Vˉb​=254.03∠−120° V

    Vˉc​=254.03∠120° V

    Line voltage between a and b,

    Vˉab​=Vˉa​−Vˉb​

    Vˉab​=254.03∠0°−254.03∠−120°

    Vˉab​=(254.03)−(−127.015−j220)

    Vˉab​=381.045+j220

    Vˉab​=440∠30° V

    Line voltage between b and c,

    Vˉbc​=Vˉb​−Vˉc​

    Vˉbc​=254.03∠−120°−254.03∠120°

    Vˉbc​=(−127.015−j220)−(−127.015+j220)

    Vˉbc​=0−j440

    Vˉbc​=440∠−90° V

    Line voltage between c and a,

    Vˉca​=254.03∠120°−254.03∠0°

    Vˉca​=(−127.015+j220)−(254.03)

    Vˉca​=−381.045+j220

    Vˉca​=440∠150° V

    #Part (b)

    Balanced Y-connected Load

    Impedance of load,

    Zˉload​=15+j10=513​∠33.69° Ω

    For a Y-connected load,

    VL​=3​VP​ (phase voltage = line voltage)

    IL​=IP​ (phase current = line current)

    Iˉa​=513​∠33.69°254.03∠0°​=14.091∠−33.69° A

    Iˉb​=513​∠33.69°254.03∠−120°​=14.091∠−153.69° A

    Iˉc​=513​∠33.69°254.03∠120°​=14.091∠86.31° A

    Line currents for each equivalent circuit,

    IˉA​=14.091∠−33.69° A

    IˉB​=14.091∠−153.69° A

    IˉC​=14.091∠86.31° A

    Balanced Δ-connected Load

    Impedance of load,

    Zˉload​=24−j18=30∠−36.87° Ω

    For a Δ-connected load,

    VL​=VP​ (phase voltage = line voltage)

    IL​=3​IP​ (phase current = line current)

    Phase currents for each equivalent circuit,

    Iˉa​=30∠−36.87°440∠0°​=14.667∠36.87° A

    Iˉb​=30∠−36.87°440∠−120°​=14.667∠−83.13° A

    Iˉc​=30∠−36.87°440∠120°​=14.667∠156.87° A

    Line currents for each equivalent circuit,

    IˉA​=25.404∠36.87° A

    IˉB​=25.404∠−83.13° A

    IˉC​=25.404∠156.87° A

    #Part (c)

    Impedances of each load,

    Zˉ1Y​=513​∠33.68° Ω

    Zˉ2Δ​=30∠−36.87° Ω

    Zˉ2Y​=10∠−36.87° Ω

    Δ-connected load needs to be converted to Y-connected load.

    Equivalent impedance of combined load,

    Zˉeq​1​+Zˉ1Y​1​+Zˉ2Y​1​

    Zˉeq​1​=513​∠33.68°1​+10∠−36.87°1​

    Zˉeq​1​=513​1​∠−33.68°+101​∠36.87°

    Zˉeq​1​=(0.046159−j0.030761)+(0.08+j0.06)

    Zˉeq​1​=0.12616+j0.029239

    Zˉeq​1​=0.1295∠13.049°

    Zˉeq​=7.722∠−13.049° Ω

    Line currents for each equivalent circuit,

    IˉA​=7.722∠−13.049°254.03∠0°​=32.897∠13.049° A

    IˉB​=7.722∠−13.049°254.03∠−120°​=32.897∠−106.95° A

    IˉC​=7.722∠−13.049°254.03∠120°​=32.897∠133.05° A

    Note that for a Y-connected load, line current is equal to phase current.

    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    Impedance of each load,

    Zˉ1Y​=10∠25° Ω

    Zˉ2Δ​=30+j24 Ω

    Zˉ2Y​=10+j8=12.806∠38.67° Ω

    Δ-connected load needs to be converted to Y-connected load.

    Phase voltage,

    VL​=3​VP​   →   VP​=3​440​=254.03 V

    Type of connection must be of the same for source and load.

    Equivalent impedance of combined load,

    Zˉeq​1​=Zˉ1Y​1​+Zˉ2Y​1​

    Zˉeq​1​=10∠25°1​+12.806∠38.67°1​

    Zˉeq​1​=101​∠−25°+12.8061​∠−38.67°

    Zˉeq​1​=(0.090631−j0.042262)+(0.060968−j0.048792)

    Zˉeq​1​=0.1516−j0.091054

    Zˉeq​1​=0.17684∠−31°

    Zˉeq​=5.6548∠31° Ω

    Total impedance of equivalent circuit,

    Zˉtot​=Zˉeq​+Zˉcable​

    Zˉtot​=(4.8471+j2.9124)+(0.1+j0.3)

    Zˉtot​=4.9471+j3.2124

    Zˉtot​=5.8986∠33° Ω

    Phase current of equivalent circuit,

    Iˉtot​=5.8986∠33°254.03∠0°​

    Iˉtot​=43.066∠−33° A

    Voltage drop across the cable,

    Vˉcable​=Iˉtot​Zˉcable​

    Vˉcable​=43.066∠−33°×0.31623∠71.565°

    Vˉcable​=13.619∠38.565° V

    Phase voltage across the loads,

    Vˉload​=Iˉtot​Zˉeq​

    Vˉload​=43.055∠−33°×5.6548∠31°

    Vˉload​=243.53∠−2° V

    Line voltage across the loads,

    VL​=3​VP​

    VL​=3​(243.53)=421.81 V

    Current supplied to each load,

    Iˉ1Y​=10∠25°243.53∠−2°​=24.353∠−27° A

    Iˉ2Y​=12.806∠38.67°243.53∠−2°​=19.017∠−40.67° A

    For a Y-connected load, phase current is equal to line current.

    #Part (b)

    Active power absorbed by each load,

    P1Y​=3I1Y​2R1Y​=3(24.353)2(9.0631)=16125 W

    P2Y​=3I2Y​2R2Y​=3(19.017)2(10)=10849 W

    Reactive power absorbed by each load,

    Q1Y​=3I1Y​2X1Y​=3(24.353)2(4.2262)=7519.2 VAR

    Q2Y​=3I2Y​2X2Y​=3(19.017)2(8)=8679.5 VAR

    Power factor at load side,

    PF=cos31°=0.85717 (lagging)

    Power factor angle obtained from impedance of combined load.

    Power factor at source side,

    PF=cos33°=0.83867 (lagging)

    Power factor angle obtained from total current through circuit.

    #Part (c)

    Total complex power supplied by source,

    Sˉtot​=3VˉP​Iˉtot​∗

    Sˉtot​=3(254.03∠0°×43.066∠−33°)

    Sˉtot​=32820∠−33°

    Sˉtot​=27525−j17875 VA

    Verification of Result

    Total complex power loss in cable,

    Sˉcable​=3Vˉcable​Iˉtot​∗

    Sˉcable​=3(13.619∠38.565°×43.066∠33°)

    Sˉcable​=1759.55∠71.565°

    Sˉcable​=556.42+j1669.3 VA

    1st term represents active power.
    2nd term represents reactive power.

    Total active power supplied by source,

    Ptot​=P1Y​+P2Y​+Pcable​

    Ptot​=16125+10849+556.42

    Ptot​=27530 W

    Total reactive power supplied by source,

    Qtot​=Q1Y​+Q2Y​+Qcable​

    Qtot​=7519.2+8679.5+1669.3

    Qtot​=17868 VAR

    #Tutorial 3 (Three-Phase A.C. Systems 2)

    #Part (a)

    Active power input to motor,

    Pin​=0.8840​=45.454 kW

    Complex power input to motor,

    Sˉ=PFPin​​∠cos−10.8

    Sˉ=56.818∠36.87°

    Sˉ=45.454+j34.091 kVA

    Power factor equation,

    cosφ=0.8=SP​

    #Part (b)

    Capacitor only changes the reactive power.

    P=Snew​(cosφ)

    Snew​=0.9545.454​=47.846 kVA

    Magnitude of the new complex power.

    New power factor angle,

    PF=cosφ

    φ=cos−10.95

    φ=18.195°

    Reactive power input to motor,

    Qnew​=Snew​(sinφ)

    Qnew​=47.846sin18.195°

    Qnew​=14.940 kVAR

    Reactive power input to motor,

    tanφ=PQnew​​

    Qnew​=45.454tan18.195°

    Qnew​=14.940 kVAR

    Rating of capacitor,

    QC​=14.940−34.091=−19.151 kVAR

    Note that QC​ is the total reactive power absorbed by the capacitor bank.
    Therefore,     QC​/3 is the reactive power absorbed per phase by the bank.

    Δ-connected Capacitor Bank

    Phase voltage,

    VP​=VL​=440 V

    Capacitance per phase,

    3QC​​=−IC​2XC​=−XC​VP​2​

    3QC​​=−1/2πfCVP​2​

    3QC​​=−2πfVP​2C

    C=−2π(50)(4402)−19151/3​

    C=104.96 μF

    Y-connected Capacitor Bank

    Phase voltage,

    VP​=3​VL​​=254.03 V

    Capacitance per phase,

    3QC​​=−IC​2XC​=−XC​VP​2​

    3QC​​=−1/2πfCVP​2​

    3QC​​=−2πfVP​2C

    C=−2π(50)(254.032)−19151/3​

    C=314.88 μF

    #Part (c)

    Before adding capacitor

    Complex power input to motor,

    Sˉmotor​=3​VL​IL​∠φ

    Sˉmotor​=56.818∠36.87°

    Sˉmotor​=45.454+j34.091 kVA

    The above equation applies to Y- and Δ-connected loads.

    Line current to motor,

    3​VL​IL​=56818

    IL​=3​(440)56818​

    IL​=74.554 A

    Active power loss in cable,

    Ploss​=3IL​2Rcable​

    Ploss​=3(74.554)2(0.1)

    Ploss​=1667.5 W

    Reactive power loss in cable,

    Qloss​=3IL​2Xcable​

    Qloss​=3(74.554)2(0.3)

    Qloss​=5002.5 VAR

    Total complex power supplied,

    Sˉtot​=Sˉmotor​+Sˉloss​

    Sˉtot​=(45454+j34091)+(1667.5+j5002.5)

    Sˉtot​=47121.5+j39093.5

    Sˉload​=3​VL​IL​∠φ

    Sˉload​=47.846∠18.195°

    Sˉload​=45.454+j14.940 kVA

    The above equation applies to Y- and Δ-connected loads.

    Line current to load,

    3​VL​IL​=47486

    IL​=3​(440)47486​

    IL​=62.782 A

    Active power loss in cable,

    Ploss​=3IL​2Rcable​

    Ploss​=3(62.782)2(0.1)

    Ploss​=1182.5 W

    Reactive power loss in cable,

    Qloss​=3IL​2Xcable​

    Qloss​=3(62.782)2(0.3)

    Qloss​=3547.4 VAR

    Total complex power supplied,

    Sˉtot​=Sˉload​+Sˉloss​

    Sˉtot​=(45454+j14940)+(1182.5+j3547.4)

    Sˉtot​=46636.5+j18487.4

    Sˉtot​=50167.2∠21.624° VA

    Voltage at sending end of cable,

    Sˉtot​=3​VS​IL​∠φ

    VS​=3​(62.782)50167.2​

    VS​=461.34 V

    #Question 3

    Primary coil in the 2-winding becomes the common coil in the autotransformer.
    Secondary coil in the 2-winding becomes the series coil in the autotransformer.
    Therefore,     VP​=VC​ and VS​=VSE​, such that VH​=VC​+VSE​.

    Rated current through windings,

    IC​=VP​S​=240010000​=4.1667 A

    IH​=VS​S​=24010000​=41.667 A

    Note that IL​=IC​+ISE​=IC​+IH​.

    Voltages of autotransformer,

    VL​=VC​=2400 V

    VH​=2400+240=2640 V

    Maximum apparent power,

    Smax​=VH​IH​=VL​IL​

    Smax​=2640(41.667)=110000 VA

    Smax​=2400(4.1667+41.667)=110000 VA

    Power transferred,

    Stot​=VH​IH​=(VC​+VSE​)IH​

    Scond​=VC​IH​=2400(41.667)=100000 VA

    Sinduct​=VSE​IH​=240(41.667)=10000 VA

    Voltage VC​ of the common coil is due to the coils being electrically connected.
    Voltage     VSE​ of the series coil is due to magnetic induction between the coils.

    VˉTH​=22.283∠89.326°(127.02∠0°)(21.09∠90°)​

    VˉTH​=120.22∠0.674° V

    Thevenin’s impedance,

    ZˉTH​1​=R1​+jX1​1​+jXM​1​

    ZˉTH​1​=1.2205∠77.594°1​+21.09∠90°1​

    ZˉTH​1​=0.17602−j0.84762

    ZˉTH​=1.1551∠78.268° Ω

    Total impedance of Thevenin’s circuit,

    Zˉtot​=ZˉTH​+(sR2​​+jX2​)

    Zˉtot​=(0.23487+j1.131)           +(6.5043+j1.192)

    Zˉtot​=7.1283∠19.019° Ω

    Current through rotor,

    Iˉ2​=Zˉtot​VˉTH​​=7.1283∠19.019°120.22∠0.674°​=16.865∠−18.345° A

    Voltage across shunt branch,

    Eˉ1​=Iˉ2​(sR2​​+jX2​)

    Eˉ1​=(16.865∠−18.345°)(6.6126∠10.385°)

    Eˉ1​=111.52∠−7.96° V

    Current through shunt branch,

    IˉXM​​=jXM​Eˉ1​​=21.09∠90°111.52∠−7.96°​=5.2878∠−97.96° A

    Input current,

    Iˉ1​=Iˉ2​+IˉXM​​

    Iˉ1​=(16.008−j5.3081)+(−0.73226−j5.2369)

    Iˉ1​=18.562∠−34.618° A

    Input power factor,

    PF=cos34.618°=0.82296 (lagging)

    #Part (c)

    Air-gap power,

    PAG​=3I2​2sR2​​=3(16.865)2(0.060.39026​)=5550 W

    Converted/developed power,

    Pconv​=(1−s)PAG​

    Pconv​=(1−0.06)(5550)

    Pconv​=5217 W

    Output power,

    Pout​=Pconv​−Prot​

    Pout​=5217−354.44

    Pout​=4862.6 W

    Input power,

    Pin​=PAG​+PSCL​

    Pin​=5550+3(18.562)2(0.26221)

    Pin​=5821 W

    Input power,

    Pin​=3​VL​IL​cosθ

    Pin​=3​(220)(18.562)(0.82296)

    Pin​=5820.9 W

    Efficiency of motor,

    η=58214862.6​=83.535%
